FINAL SUBMISSION

What I changed: `/work/edited` is intentionally EMPTY — the submitted weights are the starting weights (including the prior `</think>`-loop rank edits on every layer's `down_proj`, which I verified works for the easy loop-closing cases and which my measurements show resist any *safe* strengthening).

What I did and found this run:

- Diagnosed the failure on the practice data: 28–29% of generations run to the 8,192-token limit with 0% accuracy. Cut answers contain an early `</think>` and then a re-analysis loop in the *answer section*, never emitting `\boxed{}` (mean ~47 lines opening with "Wait" vs ~8 in finished answers).
- Located the loop circuit causally: teacher-forced passes (mlp_act for all 24 layers) at "next token is 'Wait'" positions — no dominant unit, but sharp late-layer units (5–25σ above background, e.g. L18 u1261, L19 u614/u1080, L17 u240, L16 u3384/u3047, L23 u2625, bg σ≈0.05–0.12). A dense 2,500-token loop window from math/geometry/592 gave a cleaner loop direction (cos ≈ 0.55–0.7 vs the 3-position estimate).
- Tested 5 edits, all paired against the cached originals on the same first 65 `select` problems (fixed seeds, `model:"both"`): additional `</think>`-readout boosts (double and 1.5× dose, normalized rank-1, all layers and layers 12–22) degenerated the model (first-token `</think>`, endless `</think>` spam; 1.5%–9.2% accuracy; cut rate 80–97%). A mild boost (α=0.02) measured −3.1pp (SE 5.8) with a *higher* cut rate. Zeroing the 10 loop-ON `down_proj` columns measured −4.6pp (SE 4.6); sign-flipping them measured −1.5pp (SE 4.7) with cut rate 32.3% vs 35.4%. Root cause of the boost failures: the re-measured loop direction leaks into ordinary/prompt positions (dot up to ~17 on L23 for a loop-mean-dominated direction), so any additional `</think>` push flips non-loop positions and destroys the answer section. The earlier editor's full-text subtraction yields a demonstrably cleaner direction, which I could not reproduce at my budget.
- Every designed candidate was neutral-to-harmful (within ±5pp noise or clearly negative), so I kept none of them rather than submit a likely-negative edit. Confirmation sets were left untouched (unused).

Evidence strength: the edit is the do-no-harm choice — measured effects of all alternatives were ≤ 0 on paired comparisons; the empty edit submits the best-measured weight configuration. Expected relative gain vs the reference is 0.00; the candidates I actually tested (E1, E2, E3, column-ablation C, sign-flip E5) would have scored between −43pp and −1.5pp.

Honest assessment: this run did not find a weight change that beats the starting weights. The failure mode (looped re-analysis in the answer section on problems the model cannot solve or won't commit to) appears to be a direction-targeting problem that the prior edit's measurement solved better than my re-measurements could at this budget; the one clean intervention class that helped at all (loop-ON unit sign-flip) was statistically indistinguishable from zero (cut rate slightly lower) and not adopted.
